title: Letter from the Governor to Baroness Noakes DBE
summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey responded on 6 March 2026 to the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee's report on private markets, announcing the FPC's Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) exercise to test the ecosystem under stress. The letter reveals UK banks hold £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged corporates backed by finance sponsors—equivalent to 8% of wholesale portfolio committed limits. The FPC also lowered its system-wide Tier 1 capital benchmark by one percentage point to around 13% of risk-weighted assets.
key_points: The FPC is conducting a Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) exercise, with firm engagement and analysis expected to largely complete in 2026 and a final report in early 2027
UK banks have an estimated £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and highly-leveraged corporates backed by finance sponsors
This £173bn exposure is equivalent to 8% of UK banks' total committed limits across their wholesale portfolios
The exposure breakdown includes private equity, private credit, infrastructure, real assets, real estate, and venture capital
The FPC lowered the system-wide Tier 1 capital benchmark from approximately 14% to 13% of risk-weighted assets, reflecting reduced systematism of some banks and improved risk measurement

Participants in the PM SWES include alternative asset managers, asset managers with public markets focus, private equity and credit funds, banks, and institutional investors such as insurers and pension funds
why_it_matters: Private markets have grown significantly over two decades in the UK but have not been tested by macroeconomic stress at their current size. This letter confirms regulators are actively working to understand systemic interconnections and vulnerabilities before a stress event occurs. The £173bn exposure figure provides concrete quantification of bank entanglement with the private markets ecosystem, which has implications for credit availability and financial stability if valuations compress.
market_structure_context: The letter establishes a framework for understanding systemic risk in private markets, which represent a growing segment of UK financial intermediation. The PM SWES exercise aims to map complex interconnections between alternative asset managers, banks, and institutional investors. The capital benchmark reduction to 13% RWA signals the FPC's assessment that the banking system is appropriately capitalized given evolving risk profiles.
